Subject: Revshare split & order form mapping — need alignment

Rafael / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the call last week. We reviewed the draft partner paper and the proposed order form mapping and flagged two items on our side that block marketplace activation:

1) Pass-through / tax handling: Nimbus needs gross pass-through for taxes collected via the marketplace (we cannot net these).
2) Revshare allocation: the marketplace expects a 60/40 split (Nimbus/Partner) to align with our internal reseller program. The draft shows 70/30 which creates a gap in our payouts and reporting.

For context, attached is our current marketplace Order Form mapping (Nimbus_OrderForm_Mapping.xlsx). Key asks: can Redwood accept the 60/40 split for customers booked via Nimbus' marketplace listing, and can the Order Form include a simple split schedule so billing can reconcile automatically?

Separately, our procurement/legal team will want:
- An audit window for pass-through reconciliation (we'd prefer 24 months of retention)
- A short carveout so marketplace fees are excluded from indemnity caps if there's proven third-party tax liability

Can we get alignment on these points or schedule a 30-minute call this week?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Partner Integrations
Nimbus Cloud

Rafael / Kim / Ben —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the partner paper redline and the Nimbus mapping. High-level legal positions and proposed language:

1) Defined terms: introduce a "Marketplace Fees" definition to distinguish (a) amounts collected by the marketplace (taxes, marketplace transaction fees) and (b) Revenue subject to revshare. That lets us carve taxes/third-party fees out of revenue calculations.

2) Revshare mechanics: accept a pilot-specific 60/40 split for "Marketplace Sales" provided Nimbus confirms the marketplace transaction IDs are present on the invoice and the Order Form includes a boolean flag tacked to each line item ("MarketplaceOrigin=true").

3) Audit and retention: propose an audit right limited to once per 12 months, scoped to records strictly necessary to validate revshare amounts, with a mutually agreed third-party auditor if requested. We will hold reconciliation evidence for 18 months on our side; Nimbus asked for 24 months — recommend we agree to 18 months for Redwood and require Nimbus to retain 24 months and provide copies on request.

4) Indemnity carveout: Redwood will exclude marketplace-collected taxes and third-party marketplace fees from indemnity caps where Nimbus can show direct assessment or liability. However, we cannot accept unlimited liability; propose a narrow carveout limited to direct taxes actually charged to the customer and evidenced by official tax notices.

5) Billing ops note: if billing cannot accept embedded split entries we will implement a settlement CSV export (daily/weekly) with a matching process. That should be documented in the Order Form Appendix.

I've attached a cleaned redline with tracked changes: Redwood_Marketplace_PassThrough_Redline_v3.docx. Ben, please confirm the CSV columns we will provide (suggested columns: InvoiceID, MarketplaceTxID, CustomerID, LineItemID, GrossAmount, MarketplaceTax, PartnerShare, RedwoodShare, SettlementDate).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Marketplace_PassThrough_Redline_v3.docx (tracked changes)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Revshare split & order form mapping — ops feasibility

Marissa / Rafael —

Quick ops readout: our billing platform (v3) does not currently support emitting multiple settlement lines from a single invoice that are automatically posted to two payees. Two feasible approaches:

Option A (preferred long-term): embed marketplace metadata at the line-item level and have downstream accounting post split payouts into a net-settlement pass-through ledger. This requires a small schema change and 3 weeks of dev + config.

Option B (fast pilot): produce a daily Settlement CSV (OrderForm_SplitSchedule.csv) with the fields Marissa suggested. Nimbus can ingest the CSV and we will run an automated settlement that posts partner payouts separately. This preserves a single invoicing flow and keeps accounting simple.

For the pilot, Option B seems pragmatic. I'll attach an example CSV template and a small mapping guide. Rafael — if Nimbus accepts Option B for the pilot, we should put the CSV cadence (daily/weekly) in the Order Form Appendix and include a short technical attachment on the required MarketplaceTxID field.

Ben Carter
Head of Billing Ops
Attachments: OrderForm_SplitSchedule.csv (CSV template)

Rafael / Marissa / Ben —

Thank you for the thoughtful review and the practical ops option. Nimbus is prepared to accept the Option B settlement CSV approach for the initial marketplace onboarding so long as the following are included in the Order Form Appendix for the pilot:

• CSV cadence: weekly settlement exports for the first 90 days, then daily thereafter if volumes require it.
• Evidence retention: Nimbus requires Redwood to keep reconciliation evidence for 24 months. We note Redwood has proposed 18 months — for the pilot we'll accept 18 months provided Redwood commits to provide copying or export access on request (we will provide the same).
• Audit frequency: we will accept once-per-12-months audit if the scope is limited to revshare reconciliation and requires mutual agreement on auditor.
• Indemnity carveout: we can accept Redwood's narrow carveout for taxes/marketplace-collected third-party fees, but require explicit language that where Nimbus is assessed additional tax by a tax authority due to marketplace origination, Redwood will cooperate to provide any collected Marketplace Fees records to support Nimbus' defense.

If this is acceptable, can we finalize the Order Form Appendix and a short statement of work for the billing CSV schema? Proposed quick call on Wed 16 Dec at 10am PST to sign off.

Regards,
Priya Verma
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Nimbus Cloud
